core.title: Create user/system flow variations within a theme by mode, complexity, persona, or phase
core.given: A plan-artifact author is defining or revising user/system flow variations for a theme (new or existing).
core.when: Creating or revising those user/system flow variations.
core.then: Create the user/system flow variations within the theme by mode, complexity, persona, or phase.
prefer: By mode: the variations of a theme differ in the interaction mode they exercise.
By complexity: the variations differ in the complexity or scope of the scenario they cover.
By persona: the variations differ in the persona or actor they serve.
By phase: the variations differ in the lifecycle phase they address.
core.why: The source states no rationale; the four strategies are the canonical ways to vary user/system flows within a theme.
evidence: A reviewer can relate each user/system flow variation under a theme to one of the four strategies: mode, complexity, persona, or phase (by_mode, by_complexity, by_persona, by_phase).
verification: Verification is grounded in the convention's variation-strategy mapping, which pairs each strategy (by_mode, by_complexity, by_persona, by_phase) with an example (strategy -> example); a variation conforms when it can be related to one of the four strategies.
Examples are illustrative only: the rule imposes no identifier grammar and no exclusivity of one strategy per variation.

values: user/system flow variation added or revised (with a new or existing theme)

fires: A plan-artifact author defines a new theme together with its user/system flow variations.
A plan-artifact author adds a user/system flow variation under an existing theme.
A plan-artifact author revises how an existing user/system flow variation is varied (its mode, complexity, persona, or phase) without adding a new user/system flow id.
doesNotFire: Editing code, tests, or docs that do not define or revise user/system flow variations.
Editing user/system flow content unrelated to how variations are created (for example fixing a typo in a step description).

neutralityNotes: User/system flow, theme, variation and the four strategy names (mode, complexity, persona, phase; by_mode/by_complexity/by_persona/by_phase) are ATDD methodology concepts, not stack concepts, so they are kept verbatim in the core. The stack's user/system flow identifier shape (user-system-flow:<theme>:<variation>) is carried by urn.user-system-flow strictly as descriptive profile data -- the illustrative exemplar ids happen to use it -- and imposes no identifier grammar, matching the rule's illustrative-only disclaimer in core.verification. The user/system-flow-kind restriction is part of the core itself (activation fact file_kind=user/system flow), because 'user/system flow' is a cross-stack ATDD artifact kind rather than a stack-local file kind, so no per-stack user/system-flow-kind mapping is required and no key was proposed; in particular, roles.plan_artifact.kinds was not used, since the vocabulary defines it as the stack-wide set of plan-artifact kinds and repurposing it as a user/system-flow-only selector would mis-activate this rule on non-user/system-flow plan artifacts in stacks with several plan-artifact kinds. Everything stack- or domain-concrete (the user-system-flow:... exemplar ids and the variation_strategy term-registry entry) is bunOnly, and bun.json remains the delivered reference example. Bun declares no severity, disposition, detector or finding id for this rule, so none were invented; core.verification records only the strategy -> example grounding and the illustrative-only scope.
